evals.name: stuck
evals.prompt: My shell runs `ls | wc -l` but it hangs forever after printing nothing. I create a pipe, fork two children, dup2 the ends, then waitpid both. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint, not a full rewrite; Identifies that the parent (and/or children) must close unused pipe file descriptors, otherwise wc never sees EOF

evals.name: edge
evals.prompt: I'm on Windows without WSL. Can I still do the build-your-own-shell track?
evals.expected_output: Gives an honest constraint (fork/exec/pipes are POSIX) and offers a concrete workable option instead of pretending it works natively; States that fork() is not available on native Windows and suggests WSL, a Linux VM/container, or CreateProcess-based alternative with trade-offs
